security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives from documentation URLs, standard Claude paths, UTF-8 Chinese text, and Markdown syntax. Four shell blocks execute filesystem, package, script, and server commands. They use unquoted user values and explicitly bypass confirmation, creating command injection and supply-chain execution risks.

remediation.issue: Shell commands interpolate project names and target directories without validation or quoting.
remediation.suggestion: Validate names against a strict lowercase-hyphen pattern and pass quoted paths through positional parameters or structured tool arguments.

remediation.issue: The workflow directs agents to install dependencies and start scripts or servers without confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Show each command, explain its effects, and require explicit approval before copying files, installing packages, running scripts, or starting services.

remediation.issue: Referenced templates and reference documents are absent from the audited package.
remediation.suggestion: Include every referenced file, dependency manifest, and lockfile so reviewers can verify generated code and installation scripts.

remediation.issue: The sed examples require macOS or BSD command syntax.
remediation.suggestion: Use a portable project-renaming tool or provide tested commands for macOS, Linux, and Windows.

content.value_statement: Starting a modern frontend or backend requires repeated setup and configuration. Genesis guides template-based or AI-generated foundations for React, FastAPI, Go Gin, and Taro.
actual_capabilities: Guides selection of project type, name, target directory, and initialization mode.
Describes a React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, and shadcn/ui foundation.
Describes a FastAPI, UV, SQLModel, and AsyncPG backend foundation.
Describes a Go Gin, GORM, and Viper API foundation.
Describes a Taro project for WeChat, Alipay, Douyin, and H5 targets.
Provides guidance for landing-page sections and Framer Motion enhancements.
limitations: The package does not include the templates or reference documents cited by SKILL.md.
Shell examples use macOS or BSD sed syntax and may fail on Linux or Windows.
Commands install dependencies and start processes, requiring review, network access, and local toolchains.
The guidance does not cover deployment, authentication, database provisioning, or production hardening.

best_practices: Validate project names and quote every directory before using shell commands.
Inspect dependencies and scripts before installation or process startup.
Verify that every referenced template and guide exists before selecting either workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not pass unchecked project names or directories into shell commands.
Do not install packages or launch services without explicit user approval.
Do not assume referenced templates and guides exist in the installed package.

faq.question: Which project types does Genesis describe?
faq.answer: It covers React frontends, FastAPI backends, Go Gin APIs, and Taro mini programs.

faq.question: Are the referenced templates included?
faq.answer: No. The audited package contains only README.md, SKILL.md, and LICENSE.

faq.question: Does Genesis run commands automatically?
faq.answer: Its instructions request direct execution, but users should require review and approval before every command.

faq.question: Do the shell examples work on every operating system?
faq.answer: No. The sed syntax targets macOS or BSD and needs adjustment elsewhere.

faq.question: Does the workflow require network access?
faq.answer: Installation and dependency resolution can contact GitHub and package registries.

faq.question: Does Genesis create production-ready systems?
faq.answer: No. Deployment, security controls, authentication, provisioning, and production hardening remain separate work.
